title: Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr attend Neil Aspinall’s wedding | 1968
content:
Neil Aspinall Marries Suzy Ornstein

On August 30 1968, Neil Aspinall, 26, the managing director of The Beatles Apple Corps, married 24-year-old Suzy Ornstein at Chelsea Register Office on London’s King’s Road.

The couple had known each other for just over a year, having met at a party. Suzy was the daughter of Bud Ornstein, a senior film executive and former chief executive of United Artists Pictures (UK). At the time they met, her father was the United Artists representative overseeing The Beatles’ first two films, A Hard Day’s Night and Help!.

Aspinall had been a close associate of The Beatles since their Liverpool days. He had been at school with Paul McCartney and George Harrison at the Liverpool Institute. In 1962 he fathered a son, Roag, with Mona Best, the mother of The Beatles’ original drummer Pete Best.

Aspinall had originally trained as an accountant, but became The Beatles’ driver and roadie, eventually leaving accountancy to become their full-time road manager.

Following the death of Brian Epstein in August 1967, The Beatles decided they would not appoint another manager. Instead, they turned to Aspinall to oversee their newly-established Apple Corps organisation. As its managing director, he was responsible for coordinating the activities of its various companies and remained one of the key figures in The Beatles’ business affairs during and after the reign of Allen Klein.

Aspinall wanted his wedding to be a quiet affair. The brief Register Office ceremony was attended by a small group, with Alexis ‘Magic Alex’ Mardas serving as best man and Peter Brown, the former personal assistant to Brian Epstein and a director of NEMS, giving the bride away.

Without Aspinall’s knowledge, Brown secretly arranged a reception at a nearby restaurant. The couple were greeted by friends, colleagues and many leading figures from Apple, who gathered to celebrate with champagne and an informal salad lunch served in the late afternoon.

Among the guests were Paul McCartney, Ringo Starr and Maureen Starkey, and a host of Apple and Beatles associates. They included Apple Records chief Ron Kass, Apple Films head Denis O’Dell, Mal Evans, record producer Peter Asher, Alistair Taylor, Derek Taylor, Terry Doran, Tony Bramwell, Beatles press officer Tony Barrow, and Nat Weiss, the group’s American representative from New York.

Neil and Suzy Aspinall remained married until his death in March 2008. They had three daughters and a son together.

Chelsea Register Office was then at 244–250 King’s Road. It moved across the road to Chelsea Old Town Hall in 1978. Other celebrity weddings taking place there included Judy Garland and Mickey Deans in 1969, and Marc Bolan and June Chile in 1970.

Following the wedding reception, Paul McCartney completed the recording of ‘Dear Prudence’ at London’s Trident Studios.
